sections.title: Sandpile avalanches in two dimensions are finite
sections.abstract: In the stationary abelian sandpile on Z^2, the author proves that adding one grain almost surely stabilizes, despite the divergent two-dimensional random-walk Green function, with a polylogarithmic upper bound on the chance the avalanche reaches distance R.
sections.claimed_result: The author proves almost-sure stabilization after adding a grain at the origin and bounds the radius tail by C(log(R+2))^{-a} for constants a>0 and C<infinity; the proof reduces to a uniform-spanning-tree estimate handled by a multiscale electrical argument.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Infinite-volume stationary state obtained as the local limit of uniform recurrent sandpiles on wired boxes in Z^2; one grain is added at the origin.
sections.unique_caveat: The tail estimate is an upper bound, not a sharp asymptotic; the proof and linked Lean artifact were not independently checked.

sections.title: A Lean Formalization of the Hamilton--Perelman Proof of Thurston's Geometrization Conjecture
sections.abstract: The authors formalize the Hamilton–Perelman Ricci-flow proof of geometrization and state a Lean theorem producing prime factors, incompressible-torus decompositions, and complete geometric structures on the resulting pieces.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report a Lean formalization of geometrization for connected, closed, oriented smooth 3-manifolds, yielding prime factors and torus decompositions whose pieces have complete Thurston geometries.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Input: a connected, closed, oriented smooth 3-manifold. The torus family need not be the canonical JSJ family; finite volume is asserted only for hyperbolic pieces.
sections.unique_caveat: Independent reproduction of the pinned formal artifact and its dependencies remains a useful verification step.

sections.title: The Tate Conjecture for Ordinary Calabi-Yau Threefolds
sections.abstract: Using canonical lifts, the author proves the integral geometric Tate conjecture for ordinary Calabi–Yau threefolds over finite fields, with related divisor-class results in higher dimensions.
sections.claimed_result: The author proves the integral geometric Tate conjecture for ordinary and strict 1-ordinary Calabi–Yau threefolds; in higher dimensions the result is for divisor classes under 2-ordinarity and a cohomology vanishing condition.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Smooth, projective, geometrically irreducible Calabi–Yau varieties over finite fields; threefold and higher-dimensional conclusions have distinct ordinarity hypotheses and scopes.
sections.unique_caveat: This is not a result for arbitrary Calabi–Yau varieties; ordinarity and related hypotheses are essential.

sections.title: A counterexample to Nirenberg's conjecture on closed asymptotic curves
sections.abstract: The authors construct a negatively curved embedded annulus in R^3 with two closed asymptotic curves, contradicting the stated 1962 conjecture.
sections.claimed_result: A smooth embedded annulus with negative Gauss curvature in its interior and specified tangent-plane, strictly convex boundary curves contains two closed asymptotic curves.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: A surface in Euclidean R^3 with the abstract's stated curvature and boundary geometry.
sections.unique_caveat: The counterexample does not classify closed asymptotic curves on negatively curved surfaces in general.

sections.title: The Bernstein problem in higher dimensional Heisenberg groups
sections.abstract: For each sub-Riemannian Heisenberg group H^n, n>=2, the authors prove existence of a global perimeter minimizer with smooth non-characteristic entire intrinsic-graph boundary that is not a vertical hyperplane.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove existence of a nonvertical entire intrinsic graph that globally minimizes perimeter in every H^n with n>=2.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Sub-Riemannian perimeter minimization in higher-dimensional Heisenberg groups.
sections.unique_caveat: This does not settle the classical Euclidean Bernstein problem or other sub-Riemannian settings.

sections.title: On some rigidity results for high-dimensional confoliations
sections.abstract: The authors prove an obstruction to contact regions for c-symplectic confoliations in odd dimensions, derive a 5D Reeb-stability analogue under stronger assumptions, and construct strong symplectic foliations that cannot be contact approximated in two specified senses.
sections.claimed_result: The paper establishes contact-region and contact-approximation results for specified c-symplectic confoliations, including examples in every odd ambient dimension.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The stated c-symplectic confoliation and contact-approximation hypotheses; the five-dimensional Reeb-stability analogue uses stronger assumptions.
sections.unique_caveat: The results are not blanket obstructions for all confoliations or every meaning of contact approximation.

sections.title: Constructive Bounds for the Topological Expressivity of Neural Networks
sections.abstract: The author gives constructive architecture bounds for ReLU networks to represent spaces with prescribed Betti-number patterns, shifting topological expressivity from decision boundaries to network outputs.
sections.claimed_result: The author proves sufficient architecture bounds for output spaces homotopy equivalent to wedge sums of spheres with arbitrary Betti numbers and improves bounds for products of spheres; a tighter sphere bound is conjectured.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Topological expressivity of ReLU network outputs; this is a representation result, not a claim about trained performance.
sections.unique_caveat: The tighter architecture bound is conjectural, and representability does not ensure an optimizer will find such a network.
